transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. Some weeks... I barely even touch my dinner. And then other nights, I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets long after everyone else has gone to bed. It's just really inconsistent, and I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Well, like I was just saying about my eating being all over the place... my weight just kind of goes up and down with it. Because I have those weeks where I barely touch my food, and then those nights where I'm up late snacking on crackers and sweets... my weight just hasn't been stable. So, yeah, it fluctuates depending on how my appetite is doing.
Do you ever feel like you're eating very large amounts of food in a short period of time, and can't stop yourself?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's not like I'm eating massive amounts all at once or feel like I can't stop. It's just... I'll have some crackers, maybe a few cookies, just grazing late at night. I never feel out of control with it, it's just more than I usually eat.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating those late-night snacks?

Not really about the snacks, no. I mean, maybe a little, but... the guilt I feel is usually about other things. 

I can spend hours just... replaying really small things in my head. Like if I buy an expensive tube of pigment, or if I snap at my spouse. I'll just sit there and feel like I’ve completely ruined the whole household because of it. So, yeah, I do get really guilty, just... usually not about the food.
Do you worry about gaining weight?

No, not really. I mean, I notice when my clothes fit a little differently because my weight goes up and down, but... it doesn't really bother me. I have enough other things on my mind, so my weight just isn't something I spend time worrying about.
Are you afraid of becoming fat?
No, not at all. Like I was just saying, it's really just... not something I think about. I don't have any fear of getting fat or anything like that.
Do you usually eat those late-night snacks when you're feeling stressed or upset?
No, I don't think so. It's not really tied to being stressed or upset. I think it's more just... if I happen to be up late, I get hungry. It doesn't really seem connected to my mood at all.
Do you think about your body shape or weight a lot?

No, I really don't. Um... I guess it goes back to what I was saying earlier. I just don't spend much time focusing on it at all. My shape is just my shape, so I don't really sit around thinking about it or analyzing it.
Do you think eating helps you feel better when you're not even hungry?
No, not really. I mean... I don't use food to comfort myself, if that's what you mean. If I'm not hungry, I just don't eat. It doesn't really change how I feel emotionally.
Do you think eating those late-night snacks has anything to do with how you're feeling emotionally at the time?

I really don't think it's emotional. It's just... well, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. It doesn't seem tied to my mood, it's just that some weeks I barely touch dinner at all. And then other nights, I'm just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone's gone to bed. It fluctuates a lot, but I wouldn't say it's because of how I'm feeling at the time.
Do you think there's any emotional reason why you eat at irregular times?

No, like I was just saying, I really don't think it's an emotional thing. It's just... my appetite is completely unpredictable right now. That erratic eating is actually what finally pushed me to make this appointment. I'll go through weeks where I barely touch my dinner, and then suddenly I'm the one standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else is asleep. I don't know why it changes so drastically, but I don't feel like I'm doing it because of my feelings.
Are there times when you just don't feel like eating at all, even when it's a normal meal time?

Yes, exactly. Like I was just saying a moment ago, there are definitely whole weeks where I barely touch my dinner. That's a normal meal time, but I just don't have any desire to eat. My eating has just been completely all over the place. That's really what pushed me to come in—going from having zero appetite at dinner to suddenly standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else is in bed.
Do you think you're not eating at normal meal times because you're just not interested in food?

Yeah, I suppose during those times I just lose interest in it. But like I've been saying, it doesn't stay that way. My eating is just completely all over the place, which is honestly what finally pushed me to come in and get help. I'll have those weeks where I barely touch my dinner because I just don't care about eating, and then other nights I'm standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed.
Is your lack of interest in food during certain times due to a lack of hunger or is it something else?

I think it really is just a lack of hunger. I just don't feel hungry at all during those stretches. But like I keep saying, it's that back-and-forth that finally pushed me to come in today. My eating has just been completely all over the place. I go from those weeks where I barely touch my dinner to other nights where I'm standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed.
Do you think there's something going on in your life or in your thoughts that might be contributing to these changes in your eating habits?

I don't really think so. I mean, I'm not sure. I haven't noticed any specific thoughts or big life events that trigger it. It just... happens. My mind feels okay, it's just my appetite that's completely out of whack.
Do you think your eating patterns might be related to any psychological issues you're experiencing?

I don't really know if it's psychological. I just know that what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has been all over the place. Like I mentioned, some weeks I barely touch my dinner, and then other nights I'm standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone's gone to bed. It's just very confusing.
Do you feel anxious when you're not eating at your usual times?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious. It's not a nervous feeling or anything like that. I just... I simply don't have the urge to eat during those times. I'm not sitting there worrying about missing a meal, the hunger just isn't there.
Do you think your irregular eating patterns might be related to your tendency to replay small things in your head and feel guilty about them?

I'm not sure if it's connected to my eating, honestly. But I do have that tendency. I can spend hours just replaying really small things in my head... like if I buy an expensive tube of pigment, or if I snap at my spouse over something silly. I'll just dwell on it and start to feel like I’ve completely ruined the whole household because of it. It's a really heavy feeling of guilt, I just don't know if that's what makes my appetite change.
Do you think your eating patterns might be affected by the time you spend replaying small things in your head?

I mean, I suppose it could be. Like I was just saying, I really do get stuck on those little things. If I buy that expensive paint, or if I'm short with my husband, I just replay it over and over. And when I do that, I get this awful feeling that I'm just... dragging everyone down, like I've ruined the whole household over something so small. So maybe when I'm feeling that guilty and worthless, it just kills my appetite, or makes me eat weirdly later. I just hadn't really put the two together before.
Do you think your eating patterns change when you're replaying those small things in your head and feeling guilty?

Yeah, I think they probably do. Like I mentioned, I can spend hours just going over and over those little things... like spending too much on a tube of pigment for my painting, or just being snappy with my husband. I get so caught up in it, and I start feeling like I've just completely ruined the whole household over it. When I'm stuck feeling that guilty and terrible about myself, I guess I really don't think about eating.
